title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: First $20,000 income tax exemption
sections.summary: The passage describes the long-standing exemption of the first $20,000 of chargeable income, introduced in Budget 2002, and notes changed incomes, GST and costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In that same spirit, let me turn to one specific aspect of our tax system – the long-standing provision that effectively exempts the first $20,000 of chargeable income from tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This framework was introduced in Budget 2002, at a time when GST-related rebates and personal reliefs were consolidated into the tax system to protect lower- and middle-income Singaporeans as we shifted towards greater reliance on indirect taxation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Median incomes have more than doubled, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) has increased and cost structures have shifted significantly.

sections.label: MOF reviewing the matter
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said in his round-up speech that MOF will be looking into it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister already mentioned in his round-up speech that MOF will be looking into it.

sections.label: Annual Value sets property tax
sections.summary: Under the Annual Value system, a property's tax is set by comparable rentals, including the neighbour's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Annual Value (AV) system, his property tax is set by comparable rentals, including his neighbour's.

sections.label: AV ties tax to neighbours
sections.summary: The AV system links an owner-occupier's tax to his neighbours' self-interested actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The AV system yokes an owner-occupier's tax to his neighbours' self-interested actions.

sections.label: Service charge hides restaurant prices
sections.summary: Restaurants imposing a service charge can advertise prices almost 17% lower than what customers actually pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Restaurants that impose a service charge can advertise prices almost 17% lower than what customers actually pay.

sections.label: Hotels and takeaway exemption rationale
sections.summary: The takeaway rationale cannot explain why hotels also enjoy the same exemption, since there is no takeaway hotel room.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And this takeaway rationale cannot explain why hotels also enjoy the same exemption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is no such thing as a takeaway hotel room.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus supports SMEs
sections.summary: The passage states that fiscal resilience is the greatest support for SMEs and that a fiscal surplus was achieved this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This fiscal resilience is itself the greatest support for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This year we have achieved a fiscal surplus.

sections.label: Balancing reserves and SME support
sections.summary: It asks how the Government will balance replenishing reserves and maintaining discipline with increasing support for SME transformation, digitalisation and internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, when utilising the fiscal supplies, how will the Government balance replenishing reserves and maintaining discipline while also increasing support for SMEs for transformation, digitalisation and internationalisation, so that businesses become more competitive in an uncertain environment?

sections.label: Reviewing regulatory requirements across industries
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will review rules across industries to increase operational flexibility and shorten processing times for regulatory outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: At a time when companies are already squeezed by rising costs and fierce competition, streamlining regulatory requirements would materially ease these burdens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I therefore ask whether the Government will undertake a review of rules across industries and verticals to identify opportunities to increase operational flexibility and shorten processing times for regulatory outcomes.

sections.label: ASEAN Single Window and tax system
sections.summary: It asks what more will be done through the ASEAN Single Window, and notes that about 35% of Singaporeans and PRs pay no personal income tax.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: It enables secure electronic exchange of trade documents, speeds up cross‑border clearance and supports deeper economic integration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Hence, could the Government set out what more will be done to expand cross‑border trade and reduce friction through the ASEAN Single Window?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, much has been said about our recent Budget surplus and how we can share this gain with Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But the MOF Occasional Paper released earlier shows that about 35% of Singaporeans and PRs do not pay personal income tax, and our personal income tax system is already largely progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Budget 2016, the relief cap was reduced from $100,000 to $80,000 from Year of Assessment (YA) 2018 to ensure that higher-income individuals pay more tax.

sections.label: Tax credit for NSman and caregiver
sections.summary: It suggests a $2,500 tax credit, comprising $1,500 for an NSman and $1,000 for a caregiver, instead of tax relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For a single-income household earning about $12,000 a month, after claiming the reliefs, tax payable would still be around $6,000 to $7,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I suggest a modest $2,500 tax credit, comprising $1,500 for an NSman and $1,000 for a caregiver instead of tax relief.

sections.label: Government procurement and vendors
sections.summary: It states that the Government spends close to $30 billion a year on procurement, contracting with close to 8,000 vendors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In my engagements with the private sector, including with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF), it is clear that our Government is a key player in our corporate ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It spends close to $30 billion a year on procurement, contracting with close to 8,000 vendors.

sections.label: Faster payments for contracts
sections.summary: Proposes faster payments through quicker payment cycles for smaller contracts and milestone-based payments for larger ones, including Progressive Wage Credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, faster payments through quicker payment cycles for smaller contracts and milestone-based payments for larger ones, including more regular payments for Progressive Wage Credits.

sections.label: Refreshing GeBIZ system
sections.summary: Proposes refreshing GeBIZ to streamline documentation, reduce repetitive submissions and make procurement more user-friendly for businesses, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Chairman, if we want businesses, especially SMEs, to work well with Government, their experience on GeBIZ must be efficient, transparent and fair.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I propose that we refresh the Government Electronic Business System (GeBIZ) to streamline documentation, reduce repetitive submissions and make procurement more user-friendly.

sections.label: Automatic bid compliance checks
sections.summary: Says the system should automatically check bids comply with Progressive Wage Model and Local Qualifying Salary requirements before awards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The system should also automatically check that bids comply with the Progressive Wage Model and Local Qualifying Salary requirements before awards are made, ensuring responsible contracting.

sections.label: Expanding TenderLite into ICT
sections.summary: Says expanding TenderLite into ICT can lower entry barriers, let smaller firms build credentials and strengthen the local tech ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: As agencies accelerate digitalisation, expanding TenderLite into ICT can lower entry barriers, allow smaller firms to build credentials progressively and strengthen our local tech ecosystem.

sections.label: Shared support for Statutory Boards
sections.summary: Asks whether pooled investment platforms or central advisory capabilities could help smaller boards achieve better risk-adjusted returns while preserving autonomy and mandates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, several Statutory Boards, including JTC, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore and our polytechnics host substantial financial resources to support their long-term missions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Is there scope for a stronger shared support, for example, pool investment platforms or enhanced central advisory capabilities could help smaller boards achieve better risk-adjusted returns, while preserving their autonomy and mandates?

sections.label: Quarterly payouts aligned with GST
sections.summary: Says businesses shared that more frequent payouts, such as quarterly disbursements aligned with GST cycles, would ease cash flow without increasing fiscal requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Businesses have shared that more frequent payouts, such as quarterly disbursements aligned with GST cycles, would ease cash flow without increasing overall fiscal requirements.

sections.label: Compensation for material scope changes
sections.summary: Recognising revision that substantially expands deliverables as legitimate grounds for additional payment would set clearer standards and reduce disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A related issue concerns compensation for material scope changes, where revision substantially expand deliverables, recognising these as legitimate grounds for additional payment would set clearer standards and reduce disputes.

sections.label: Net Investment Returns Contribution framework
sections.summary: The tax system is supplemented by the NIRC framework, which allows part of investment returns to be taken into the annual budget sustainably.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our tax system is supplemented by the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) framework that allows part of our investment returns to be taken into the annual budget in a sustainable way.

sections.label: Budget 2026 company support
sections.summary: As announced in Budget 2026, these include additional support for companies, especially SMEs, to internationalise and build AI capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As announced in Budget 2026, these include additional support for companies, especially our SMEs, to internationalise and build AI capabilities.

sections.label: MOF reviews Statutory Board finances
sections.summary: MOF reviews the financial positions of Statutory Boards to prevent excessive build-up of reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: MOF reviews the financial positions of Statutory Boards to prevent excessive build-up of reserves.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant changes
sections.summary: MOF worked with MOM, MOE and MTI to review programmes and announced changes in Budget 2025, including the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We worked closely with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), the Ministry of Education, and the Ministry of Trade and Industry to review our existing programmes and announced the key changes in Budget 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This included the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant that consolidates workforce transformation schemes under a single application channel to provide more holistic support to companies.

sections.label: Cost avoidance in development costs
sections.summary: In 2025, Government agencies with MOF and DPAP achieved total cost avoidance of at least $1.4 billion in development costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2025, Government agencies, working together with MOF and DPAP, were able to achieve a total cost avoidance of at least $1.4 billion in development costs.

sections.label: Rental data for property tax
sections.summary: Using rental data to determine Annual Value keeps annually assessed property taxes more stable and predictable for homeowners.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is not a question of using AV for rental properties and capital value for owner-occupied properties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, on this, the use of rental data to determine AV keeps property taxes, which are assessed annually, more stable and predictable for homeowners.

sections.label: Different rates for occupancy
sections.summary: Residential properties are valued by a common yardstick, but different property tax rates apply to owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied properties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While the valuation for all residential properties is determined using a common yardstick, we can and do apply different property tax rates for owner occupied and non-owner-occupied properties.

sections.label: Capital value not necessarily lower
sections.summary: Shifting to capital value as the basis for property tax assessment does not necessarily lower the assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In any case, shifting to capital value as the basis for property tax assessment does not necessarily lower the assessment.

sections.label: Licence and audit changes
sections.summary: Customs may extend certain licences from three to five years and shorten some licence waits to 30 working days, while ACRA will consult on audit exemptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For instance, Customs is considering extending the validity period of certain licences from three years to five years, so that businesses need not renew them as frequently.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Customs is also shortening the time for businesses to obtain some licences to within 30 working days, so businesses have greater certainty in their planning and operations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) will consult businesses and the audit community later this year on whether to exempt more small enterprises from having to audit their financial statements.

sections.label: Digital invoice savings estimate
sections.summary: A recent Deloitte study estimated that using digital invoices can save small businesses up to $20 per invoice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: A recent study by Deloitte estimated that using digital invoices can save small businesses up to $20 per invoice.

sections.label: Mandatory e-invoicing by 2031
sections.summary: All GST-registered businesses will be required to submit digital invoices to IRAS via InvoiceNow by April 2031, bringing on 90,000 more businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: As more businesses come onboard the InvoiceNow network, the network benefits and efficiency gains will only increase further and so in consultation with SBF and other trade associations, we are now ready to take the next step to push for greater adoption of e-invoicing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We will require all GST-registered businesses to submit digital invoices to IRAS via InvoiceNow by April 2031.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This will bring on 90,000 more businesses to the InvoiceNow network.

sections.label: Cash grants for InvoiceNow software
sections.summary: New cash grants will defray operational costs of adopting InvoiceNow-Ready software, up to $1,000 for smaller companies and $5,000 for larger companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Second, we will provide new cash grants to defray any operational costs of adopting InvoiceNow-Ready software up to $1,000 for smaller companies and up to $5,000 for larger companies.

sections.label: Resident workers paying no income tax
sections.summary: Under the current system, one in three resident workers do not pay any personal income tax at all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Under our current system, one in three resident workers do not pay any personal income tax at all.

sections.label: Tender Lite for SME tenders
sections.summary: Tender Lite was first introduced in April 2024 to simplify contract conditions of tenders up to $1 million, making them more accessible to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Tender Lite was first introduced in April 2024 to simplify the contract conditions of tenders up to $1 million, making them more accessible to SMEs.

sections.label: Streamlining contract conditions and damages
sections.summary: Contract conditions will be streamlined, removing liquidated damages clauses where possible or capping them at 10% of relevant contract value.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: First, we will streamline the number of contract conditions so that businesses find it simpler to participate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: We will remove clauses on liquidated damages where possible or cap the liquidated damages for late delivery and service performance at 10% of the relevant contract value.

sections.label: Tender Lite for ICT procurement
sections.summary: MOF will launch Tender Lite for ICT procurement from April 2026, with around 90% of Government procurement opportunities benefiting from simpler contract conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: MOF will be launching Tender Lite for ICT procurement from April 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: With Quotation and Tender Lite, around 90% of Government procurement opportunities will benefit from simpler contract conditions, making procurement more accessible to businesses, especially SMEs.

sections.label: Engagement on refreshed GeBIZ system
sections.summary: MOF will work with SBF and ASME on modes of engagement with businesses to ensure the refreshed GeBIZ system meets Government procurement and business community needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: MOF will work with SBF and ASME on the modes of engagement with businesses to ensure the refreshed GeBIZ system meets the needs of our Government procurement and business community.

sections.label: AI in GeBIZ system
sections.summary: MOF is committed to integrate AI tools into the refreshed GeBIZ system where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: MOF is committed to integrate AI tools into the refreshed GeBIZ system where possible.

sections.label: AI detecting anomalies
sections.summary: ACRA, AGD and Customs officers will better identify trends and detect anomalies like non-compliance or fraud through these tools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Through these tools, ACRA, AGD and Customs officers will be better able to identify trends and detect anomalies, such as non-compliance or fraud, that may not have been detected as quickly via more traditional methods.

sections.label: Procurement access and technology
sections.summary: Improve access to Government procurement and leverage technology to improve efficiency and strengthen governance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Improve access to Government procurement; and leverage technology to improve efficiency and strengthen governance.

sections.label: GST concession and service charges
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State said the GST concession is because service charges are variable and may be waived or reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The Senior Minister of State said that the GST concession is because the service charges are "variable and may be waived or reduced", which it may very well be, but then there is nothing stopping a coffee shop from charging 0.1% service charge to charge GST exclusive prices, which it did in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: So, that is not consistent with what IRAS subsequently did, which was to enforce it and clarify the rules because it updated its guidelines to state that the pricing exception does not apply to businesses that levy a nominal service charge without a genuine business reason, other than to avoid displaying GST inclusive prices.

sections.label: IRAS stance on nominal charges
sections.summary: IRAS takes a firm stance against businesses levying nominal service charges without genuine reason other than avoiding displaying GST inclusive prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Indeed, IRAS takes a firm stance against businesses who levy nominal service charges without genuine reason, other than to avoid displaying GST inclusive prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: As I explained in my speech, we will indeed review this and do a discussion and exploration with businesses as well as consumers, on whether or not they would prefer for us to move in a different direction.
